title: Redwood Private VPC security architecture deep dive with Northpoint Bank
summary: Deep dive on Private/VPC and on-prem deployment architecture for Redwood Private. Covered network isolation, ingress/egress controls, firewalling options, NAT and proxy strategies, private endpoints vs VPC peering, audit log forwarding, KMS/HSM integration, SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SSO/RBAC. Agreed next steps to share diagrams, SOC2 pack, and schedule a network walkthrough and pilot POC.
topics: Private endpoints / VPC peering / Transit Gateway
action_items: Alex Chen - Share Redwood SOC 2 Type II report and ISO27001 summary - due 2026-02-10
Jordan Lee - Export sample flow logs and network diagram for Northpoint Private deployment - due 2026-02-12
Raj Kumar - Provide existing firewall egress rules and approved outbound ports list - due 2026-02-11
Priya Nair - Schedule hands-on VPC walkthrough and pilot RDP/SSH connectivity test - due 2026-02-16
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO artifacts and security whitepaper
Customer to share VPC network diagram and approved egress list
Schedule 1:1 network walkthrough with Northpoint network team (Jordan+Marcus+Emily)
Agree on pilot scope and success criteria and sign SOW
transcript:
Meeting header:
14:30 UTC, Feb 05 2026 · Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood PM); Sarah Thompson (CISO), Raj Kumar (Head Cloud Ops), Emily Park (Security Architect), Marcus Hale (Network Engineer)

[00:00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I see we've got the Northpoint security crew on, appreciate you making time. The plan for the call today is to deep dive into the Private VPC/on-prem security architecture, network isolation, ingress and egress, firewalling, and how we integrate with your KMS/HSM and SIEM, does that align?

[00:00:18] Sarah (Northpoint): Yes that's perfect, Alex. We want to make sure there are no surprises around data egress, certificate handling, and that the deployment model meets our compliance needs.

[00:00:28] Jordan (Redwood): Great. I'll start with a high-level diagram and then Priya can jump into the operational controls and logging.

[00:00:35] Jordan (Redwood): So in Private mode Redwood ships a control plane that can be customer-managed and a data plane that runs inside your VPC or on-prem env. The data plane nodes sit in private subnets, no public IPs, and they only talk out over configured egress paths. For VPC deployments we support private endpoints and VPC peering or transit gateway patterns.

[00:01:02] Marcus (Northpoint): Sorry Jordan, can you slow down on the private endpoints vs peering bit? We use a Transit Gateway today and we try to minimize peering.

[00:01:09] Jordan (Redwood): Sure. With private endpoints we create an interface endpoint in your account that maps directly to the Redwood service, so traffic never traverses the public internet. It's similar to AWS PrivateLink. For teams using Transit Gateway, we can attach the service VPC to your Transit Gateway instead of creating cross-account peering. Transit Gateway is often preferred at scale because it centralizes routing and simplifies egress controls.

[00:01:34] Emily (Northpoint): Do you require any specific route table changes or do you create an ENI?

[00:01:40] Jordan (Redwood): We provision interface endpoints (ENIs) in the chosen subnets and we provide a small set of required NACL and security group rules. We don't modify your route tables beyond the standard private endpoint configuration. We document the minimal changes.

[00:01:55] Raj (Northpoint): How about egress? Our compliance team limits outbound destinations, we have a proxy egress and only list certain domains.

[00:02:02] Priya (Redwood): We support routing all outbound traffic through the customer's egress proxy. The data plane respects your NAT/proxy, and we can also lock down allowed egress to specific IP ranges for Redwood-managed services. For the most locked-down option, we offer an air-gapped on-prem package where all images and packages are supplied via an internal registry.

[00:02:22] Sarah (Northpoint): Air-gap is interesting but heavy. We're more likely to do VPC with strict egress. How do you handle TLS and certificates in that case?

[00:02:30] Jordan (Redwood): All control and data plane communication is TLS 1.2/1.3 by default. For private deployments you can bring your own certificates and we support certificate rotation workflows. For customer-managed KMS we integrate with AWS KMS CMKs or customer HSMs via PKCS#11 for keys used in disk encryption and token encryption at rest.

[00:02:53] Emily (Northpoint): PKCS#11 — do you have a connector for our existing HSM vendor?

[00:02:58] Priya (Redwood): We have pre-built integrations for common HSM vendors and we work with your security team for a connector. If needed we can run a short integration proof with your vendor.

[00:03:10] Marcus (Northpoint): How do you manage secrets in pods? We already use a secrets agent that pulls from KMS.

[00:03:15] Jordan (Redwood): For Kubernetes deployments we support mounting secrets via a CSI driver that pulls from your KMS at startup, and we avoid storing secrets in plaintext on disk. The token and model keys are encrypted with customer CMKs when configured.

[00:03:28] Alex (Redwood): Quick note — customers often ask if Redwood stores any customer data outside of their VPC. For Private mode, no. Logs and artifacts can be emitted into your S3 buckets or pushed to your SIEM. We never pull data back into the Redwood-hosted control plane unless explicitly configured.

[00:03:45] Sarah (Northpoint): Good. On audit logs — we use Splunk and need near real-time forwarding. How do you surface runtime telemetry and audit logs?

[00:03:52] Priya (Redwood): We stream structured audit logs and platform metrics to your logging endpoints. For AWS we can write CloudWatch logs, or push to Kinesis Firehose to S3 or directly to your Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC). Logs include request metadata, user ids, model version, and request/response hashes — we avoid storing full sensitive payloads unless you opt into debugging mode.

[00:04:14] Raj (Northpoint): Request/response hashes are fine, but we need a tamper-evident trail for compliance. Is there log signing or immutable chaining?

[00:04:21] Jordan (Redwood): We support log integrity features — logs can be signed using a customer key and delivered to an immutable store (S3 with Object Lock) or to your SIEM with integrity metadata. We can also ship logs to a dedicated logging VPC endpoint.

[00:04:36] Emily (Northpoint): Let's talk firewalling. We run Palo Alto appliances and have strict rules about source/destination and protocols. Where does Redwood sit in that flow?

[00:04:45] Jordan (Redwood): In a typical VPC deployment the data plane instances live in private subnets behind your NGFW (if you place it there) and only speak to approved outbound endpoints. We provide the IP ranges and DNS names you need to permit. If you use Transit Gateway and central NGFW, we recommend steering traffic through that appliance. For on-prem installs, the data plane can be deployed within your DMZ or internal network depending on isolation needs.

[00:05:07] Marcus (Northpoint): Do you support source-bound firewall rules so that outbound traffic is only allowed from host X to destination Y?

[00:05:12] Priya (Redwood): Yes — we publish the exact host ENI addresses or prefix lists and you can lock down egress using security groups, NACLs, or your appliance with specific rules. We can also integrate with your service discovery so rules are maintained as nodes scale.

[00:05:27] Sarah (Northpoint): What about lateral movement? We need segmentation between customer tenant workloads on our side and any Redwood-admin tools.

[00:05:34] Jordan (Redwood): Redwood's data plane respects tenant boundaries and uses network segmentation. Management/control plane traffic is scoped to the management subnets and can be placed behind separate security groups and ACLs with dedicated routes. We recommend using separate accounts or VPCs for management vs workload plane for strongest isolation.

[00:05:50] Emily (Northpoint): On RBAC and SSO — we use Okta and SCIM provisioning. We need role mapping that ties into our existing IAM groups and ensures least privilege.

[00:05:59] Alex (Redwood): We support SAML SSO with SCIM for provisioning. Role mapping can be configured so Okta groups map to Redwood roles, and you can enforce MFA via your IdP. We also support audit logging for admin actions and role changes.

[00:06:12] Sarah (Northpoint): How do you handle service accounts used by pipelines? We need service accounts that can be rotated and audited.

[00:06:18] Jordan (Redwood): We recommend short-lived service tokens issued via your internal token service or AWS STS. Redwood supports OIDC and short-lived credentials, and we can wire token rotation to your existing secrets rotation processes.

[00:06:28] Marcus (Northpoint): A big concern is data residency — our regs require data at rest to remain in the region and not cross borders.

[00:06:35] Priya (Redwood): For Private deployments you choose the region and we pin the data plane to that region. We can also configure network policies and routing to prevent cross-region traffic and ensure egress endpoints are regional.

[00:06:46] Sarah (Northpoint): You mentioned you don't pull data back to Redwood control plane unless configured — can you confirm where metadata like request timestamps and hashes live?

[00:06:54] Jordan (Redwood): Metadata can be stored in your account or in the customer-managed database. When customers prefer, we write metadata to an S3 bucket you control. Otherwise, minimal operational telemetry goes to the Redwood control plane for platform health but that is scrubbed of PII and can be disabled.

[00:07:10] Alex (Redwood): Quick interruption — Sam from product had a question about network MTU sizing for model weights transfer during node startup, might be relevant to Marcus.

[00:07:18] Sam (Redwood): Yeah, when nodes bootstrap they pull large model artifacts from an object store. We support multi-part downloads and resume. We recommend an MTU that avoids fragmentation on your VPN links, and if you use our internal caching you can reduce cross-region transfers.

[00:07:34] Marcus (Northpoint): Good to know. We use site-to-site VPN to our colo and have 1500 byte MTU, no jumbo frames.

[00:07:40] Jordan (Redwood): That's fine. We can provide tuning guidance in the deployment doc.

[00:07:45] Sarah (Northpoint): About vulnerability management — do you provide CVE scanning of images and automatic patching?

[00:07:51] Priya (Redwood): We maintain a vulnerability program: images are scanned, we publish SBOMs, and we provide patch windows. For Private on-prem installs you can opt to control image updates; Redwood issues security advisories and we can coordinate a maintenance schedule.

[00:08:06] Emily (Northpoint): For compliance evidence, we need to review your SOC2 Type II and network penetration test results.

[00:08:12] Alex (Redwood): We'll share the SOC2 pack and recent penetration test summary under NDA. That's one of the action items.

[00:08:18] Raj (Northpoint): Monitoring — can you export metrics to our Prometheus stack?

[00:08:22] Jordan (Redwood): Yes, we can emit metrics via Prometheus exporters within the VPC, and for hosted dashboards we can push metrics to your metrics ingestion pipeline.

[00:08:30] Sarah (Northpoint): Network intrusion detection — do you support flow logs and can we feed them to our IDS?

[00:08:35] Priya (Redwood): We emit VPC flow logs and application-level audit events. We can push them to your SIEM/IDS via Firehose or HEC, or drop them into S3 for offline analysis.

[00:08:45] Emily (Northpoint): Does Redwood ever need SSH or admin access into our environment?

[00:08:49] Jordan (Redwood): Only in exceptional support cases and only with explicit approval and temporary bastion access. We use just-in-time access workflows and all sessions are recorded and audited.

[00:08:59] Marcus (Northpoint): Can you summarize the network ports and domain list you need?

[00:09:04] Alex (Redwood): Short list: outbound HTTPS (443) to Redwood control plane endpoints, optional S3/Kinesis endpoints for logging, and access to your KMS endpoints. We'll provide a concise JSON of IP ranges and service endpoints. For locked down environments we support a proxy-only model where all outbound goes through your approved proxy.

[00:09:22] Sarah (Northpoint): What about egress to model repositories — do the nodes pull models from public registries?

[00:09:27] Priya (Redwood): By default we pull model artifacts from Redwood's model registry, but for high-security environments we support an internal artifact registry or preloaded local cache. We also support forcing downloads to your internal object store.

[00:09:40] Raj (Northpoint): Ok, let's talk about encryption keys lifecycle — we need quarterly rotation and separation of duties.

[00:09:46] Jordan (Redwood): Customer-managed CMKs with rotation policies are supported. You can enforce rotation cadence and we don't hold the plaintext keys. For separation of duties, you can use HSM-backed keys and RBAC controls so only your key admins can perform rotations.

[00:09:59] Emily (Northpoint): Any SLA implications for private deployments?

[00:10:04] Alex (Redwood): Dedicated and Private deployments come with enterprise SLAs that include uptime and latency targets. We'll include the SLA language in the SOW. For maintenance windows we coordinate with your ops team.

[00:10:15] Sarah (Northpoint): Alright, a few quick clarifying questions from compliance: can we have a read-only copy of logs retained for 7 years in case of audit?

[00:10:24] Priya (Redwood): Yes, we can deliver logs to an S3 bucket with Object Lock for WORM and lifecycle policies for your retention requirements. We recommend lifecycle + Glacier for long term retention.

[00:10:35] Raj (Northpoint): Do you provide a kill-switch to stop all traffic or to isolate the cluster quickly?

[00:10:40] Jordan (Redwood): We have emergency isolation controls that can be invoked from a central console or via an API which will quiesce the data plane and revoke tokens. For customer-managed deployments, we provide runbooks for how to detach or isolate nodes at the networking layer.

[00:10:54] Alex (Redwood): Great question. We'll include the runbook in the deliverables.

[00:10:59] Sarah (Northpoint): Pricing — it matters but we'll handle that with procurement. For security calls we typically want to line up a pilot with success criteria.

[00:11:06] Alex (Redwood): Agreed. Pilot often includes a small cluster in your account, log forwarder, SOC2 review, and a short benchmark to validate latency and egress controls.

[00:11:15] Marcus (Northpoint): One last network ops question — if we scale the cluster quickly, do you expect us to adjust firewall rules?

[00:11:21] Priya (Redwood): No, we support prefix-lists and SRV records so firewall changes are minimal. We can provide a prefix-list that updates as nodes scale and integrate with AWS-managed prefix lists if you prefer.

[00:11:34] Jordan (Redwood): Also, for Kubernetes installs, we can integrate with your CNI to use stable IPs for critical services so firewall rules remain stable.

[00:11:42] Sarah (Northpoint): OK, I think that's the core. Shall we do a quick recap and action items?

[00:11:48] Alex (Redwood): Yes — recap: Redwood will share SOC2 and ISO artifacts, a concise network endpoint/IP list, sample flow logs, a deployment runbook including emergency isolation steps, and a proposed pilot SOW. Northpoint will share their VPC diagrams, firewall rules and egress proxy config, and identify the network team for the walkthrough. Action items as discussed.

[00:12:10] Sarah (Northpoint): Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

[00:12:15] Alex (Redwood): Thanks, we'll follow up by EOD with the docs and a calendar invite for the walkthrough.

[00:12:22] Jordan (Redwood): Thanks all.

[00:12:25] End of call.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker overlaps and minor mis-attributions. Some technical terms spelled phonetically (PKCS eleven instead of PKCS#11).
